subject.title: fix(codex): prefer recovered replies over stale failure banners

question: Should failed Codex conversation turns be suppressed only when a completed terminal assistant item is present, or may streamed partial deltas also replace the failure banner?
rationale: The upstream Codex contract proves failed status can coexist with assistant data, but OpenClaw's sibling projector treats deltas as provisional unless phase/completion proves terminal output; deciding whether partial deltas are deliverable user replies is a message-delivery product risk.

options.title: Require completed terminal assistant evidence
options.body: Change the collector to override failed status only for completed non-commentary assistant items or turn snapshot items and keep partial-delta-only failures as errors.

options.title: Accept partial deltas as deliverable
options.body: Maintain the current PR behavior and explicitly accept the risk that incomplete streamed text can replace a real failed-turn banner.

options.title: Pause for clearer upstream signal
options.body: Hold the PR until Codex exposes a distinct recovered-versus-fatal terminal signal that OpenClaw can consume without heuristics.

recommendation.title: Require completed terminal assistant evidence
recommendation.body: Change the collector to override failed status only for completed non-commentary assistant items or turn snapshot items and keep partial-delta-only failures as errors.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the Codex app-server bridge and has the strongest history on this exact protocol/runtime boundary.
